Slice: Tool Inventory

Intent

Shows the shed manager every tool in the shed on the Tool Inventory screen, and which of them are out on loan, to whom, and until when. It is the shed manager's working screen for tools: they add and retire tools from it, and record a tool lost when it is out and never coming back.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Tool Inventory screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per tool currently in the shed or out on loan, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Add Tool (Add Tool slice) — always offered.
    • Retire (Retire Tool slice) — offered on every listed tool that is not already retired (INV-TINV-7).
    • Mark lost (Record Tool Lost slice) — offered only on a tool that is out on loan (INV-TINV-6).

Read Model / View

  • View: Tool Inventory built from events: "Tool Added", "Neighbor Registered", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Tool Inventory screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual — an entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because each command checks its own rules when it runs.

One row per listed tool. ToolId, NeighborId and LoanId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

Field Type Source / Notes
toolId ToolId Tool Added.toolId.
name Text Tool Added.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
description Text Optional: absent when the tool was added without one. Tool Added.description.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int Tool Added.defaultCheckoutPeriodDays (1–30).
addedAt Instant Tool Added.addedAt.
onLoan Bool Derived: yes from Tool Checked Out for this tool until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan; no otherwise.
loanId LoanId Derived: Tool Checked Out.loanId while the tool is on loan; none once Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan lands. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerId NeighborId Derived: Tool Checked Out.neighborId while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerName Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.name for borrowerId while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
dueDate Date Derived: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for that loan, while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
retired Bool Derived: yes once Tool Retired is recorded for this tool. A retired row exists only while the tool is still out on loan.
canRetire Bool Derived: yes while retired is no. Returned so the screen can offer Retire (INV-TINV-7).
overdue Bool Derived: yes while the tool is on loan and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate; no otherwise (INV-TINV-9). Worked out when the inventory is read.
canMarkLost Bool Derived: same as onLoan. Returned so the screen can offer Mark lost (INV-TINV-6).

Queries

  • List the tool inventory. Takes nothing. Returns every listed tool, each with all the fields above. There is no paging: the query always returns every listed tool. Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added (addedAt); tools added at the same instant keep the order their Tool Added was recorded (INV-TINV-10).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-TINV-1: Every added tool appears in the inventory exactly once.
    • One entry per Tool Added; nothing else creates an entry.
    • Each physical item is its own tool, so two identical drills are two entries.
  • INV-TINV-2: A retired tool drops off the inventory once it is back in the shed or recorded lost.
    • A tool retired while it is in the shed drops off at once.
    • A tool retired while it is out on loan stays listed, marked retired and out, until it is returned or recorded lost. Then it drops off. This lets the shed manager record it lost if it never comes back.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it drops off too.
    • This differs from the Tool Catalog, where a tool retired while on loan drops off at once: neighbors can do nothing with it, while the shed manager may still need to record it lost.
  • INV-TINV-3: The inventory changes only when a tool is added, checked out, extended, returned, retired or recorded lost, or when a neighbor registers.
    • Neighbor Registered supplies the borrower names shown on tools that are out.
    • Holds and overdue notices leave it unchanged. Hold state is shown to neighbors on the Tool Catalog, not here.
    • A tool's details never change after it is added (see the note under Add Tool's event table). A mistake is corrected by retiring the tool and adding it again.
  • INV-TINV-4: Each entry shows the tool's name, its description when it has one, and its default checkout period.
  • INV-TINV-5: Each entry shows whether the tool is out on loan. A tool that is out also shows the borrower's name and the due date.
    • A tool is out from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost.
    • The due date moves with each extension.
    • When the tool comes back or is recorded lost, the borrower's name and due date are no longer shown on it.
  • INV-TINV-6: The inventory offers "mark lost" only on a tool that is out on loan.
    • Recording a tool lost ends its loan, retires the tool and ends its holds. It never counts as a late return for the borrower (Record Tool Lost).
  • INV-TINV-7: The inventory offers "retire" on every listed tool that is not already retired.
    • A tool retired while out on loan stays listed but is not offered "retire" again.
  • INV-TINV-8: Applying the same event twice leaves the inventory as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-TINV-9: A tool that is out shows whether its loan is overdue.
    • Overdue means today's date in the shed's local time zone is after the due date in force. It is worked out when the inventory is read; no event marks a loan overdue.
  • INV-TINV-10: Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added.
    • Tools with the same name are in the order they were added; tools added at the same instant keep the order their Tool Added was recorded.
  • INV-TINV-11: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-TINV-12: Only the shed manager can read the Tool Inventory: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool added (INV-TINV-1, INV-TINV-4, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a cordless drill, described as "18V, two batteries", with a default checkout period of 7 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill with its description and its 7-day default checkout period, in the shed, with "retire" offered and no "mark lost".
  • Tool added without a description (INV-TINV-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a ladder with no description and a default checkout period of 3 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the ladder with its 3-day default checkout period and no description.
  • Two of the same tool (INV-TINV-1)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists one cordless drill
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a second cordless drill, with its own tool ID
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists both drills as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-TINV-8)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill once
    • When: the same Tool Added for that drill is applied again
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the drill once.
  • Neighbor registers (INV-TINV-3)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the drill, in the shed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for Ana Ruiz
    • Then: no entry on the Tool Inventory changes.
  • Tool checked out (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for Ana Ruiz, and the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill, in the shed
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for Ana borrowing the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as out on loan to Ana Ruiz, the name she registered with, due 12 October, and offers "mark lost" on it.
  • Loan extended (INV-TINV-5)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for Ana's drill loan, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October.
  • Tool returned (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as in the shed, with no borrower, due date or "mark lost".
  • Tool retired (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists a cordless drill and a ladder, both in the shed
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: the cordless drill drops off the Tool Inventory, and the ladder is still listed.
  • Tool retired while out on loan (INV-TINV-2, INV-TINV-6, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder out on loan to Ben, due 20 October
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the ladder
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the ladder, marked retired and out on loan to Ben, due 20 October, with "mark lost" still offered and "retire" no longer offered.
  • Retired tool comes back (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Retired tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the hedge trimmer out on loan to Ana
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ana's hedge trimmer loan
    • Then: the hedge trimmer drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Out tool becomes overdue (INV-TINV-9)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: the inventory is read at 23:59 on 12 October, and again at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: the drill shows not overdue on the first read and overdue on the second. Nothing is recorded.
  • List order (INV-TINV-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for "Ladder", then "Cordless drill", then a second "Cordless drill"
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: the order is the first "Cordless drill", the second "Cordless drill", then "Ladder".
  • Holds and notices don't change it (INV-TINV-3)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben on the drill, and later Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the drill's entry is unchanged.
  • Listing the inventory
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill (in the shed) and the ladder (out on loan to Ben, due 20 October)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: both tools are returned with all their fields, with no paging.
  • Not signed in (INV-TINV-11)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: the tool inventory is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-TINV-12)
    • Given: a neighbor is signed in, without the shed-manager role
    • When: the tool inventory is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see the tool inventory." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-TINV-11).
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-TINV-12).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-TINV-11
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can see the tool inventory. INV-TINV-12
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-TINV-8). A Tool Added, Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Tool Returned, Tool Retired or Tool Lost applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for a tool that is no longer listed: under the rules above, a Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost can reach this view for a tool that is no longer listed only as a replay of an event already applied. It changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, "mark lost" on a tool that has just been returned). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Tool Inventory is the shed manager's screen; neighbors see tools on the Tool Catalog instead. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager (INV-TINV-12), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-TINV-11).
  • PII & compliance: shows a borrower's name while they have a tool out. It never shows their email. The name stops being shown on that tool once the loan ends.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId.
    • All but Tool Added are specified in slices not yet written in depth. These names are this view's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Add Tool, Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":1,"name":"Register Neighbor","x0":289.76,"x1":433.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Register Neighbor

Intent

Let a neighbor join the tool shed by signing themselves up, so they can borrow tools. Signing up records the neighbor's name and the email address the shed uses to reach them. A new neighbor is active and can borrow straight away.

Trigger & Actor

A person who wants to join, from the Sign Up screen. They sign themselves up; the shed manager doesn't enroll neighbors. Someone whose earlier account is closed may sign up again here, as a new account. Once signed up, the neighbor signs in outside the model, and sign-in supplies their neighbor ID for every later action; it resolves a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.

Command / Input

Command: Register Neighbor

A NeighborId is a UUID. Text fields have leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed; text that is empty after that counts as absent.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new account, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different account already registered (INV-REG-7).
name Text yes Trimmed. Must not then be empty (INV-REG-3), and at most 100 characters (INV-REG-10). Need not be unique (INV-REG-9).
email Text yes Trimmed. Must not then be empty (INV-REG-3), at most 254 characters (INV-REG-10), and shaped like an email address (INV-REG-11). Must not be held by another account under INV-REG-4, compared ignoring case. Kept as typed.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Sign Up @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Registered → context Neighbors Read by: Neighbors and My Account (their own slices, right after this one); and, for the neighbor's name and email, Tool Inventory (name only), Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command. Identifies the account everywhere from here on.
name Text yes From the command, trimmed.
email Text yes From the command, trimmed. The account's email until a later Neighbor Email Changed replaces it.
registeredAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the sign-up date.

The event records a fact that never changes. A later email change is its own event; the name is never changed.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Registered starts the new account's entry in two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • Neighbors (slices/neighbors.md) lists the new neighbor to the shed manager as active.
  • My Account (slices/my-account.md) shows the new neighbor their account.

Both are eventually consistent: the new account appears once each view has caught up with Neighbor Registered.

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor signs themselves up; the shed manager does not enroll neighbors. Every account starts active: Neighbor Registered is the only event that starts an account, and suspension and closure come later, from other slices. The Neighbors view shows a new account as active (INV-NBRS-2), and Check Out Tool lends to it under its usual rules.

  • INV-REG-3: Sign-up requires a name and an email address.
    • The shed emails neighbors, and only by email: overdue notices to borrowers and pickup notices to holders both go to this address.
    • A name or email that is empty, or only whitespace, is missing.
  • INV-REG-4: A sign-up is refused if its email belongs to an account that is not closed, or to a closed account that was suspended when it was closed.
    • An account's email is its current one: the email it registered with, or the latest Neighbor Email Changed for it. An email an account has changed away from belongs to no one.
    • Emails are compared ignoring case: Ana@Example.org and ana@example.org are the same address. The email is kept as typed.
    • Whether a closed account was suspended when it was closed is read from its Neighbor Account Closed (whileSuspended), never worked out from earlier suspensions and reinstatements.
    • One account per email. A closed account's email can be used again, so a neighbor who left can come back with the same address.
    • An account closed while suspended keeps its email for good, so a suspended neighbor can't get around the suspension by closing their account and signing up again with the same email. A suspended neighbor can't change their email (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email), so that email is the one they were suspended under.
    • A sign-up with a different email is accepted, even from someone whose earlier account was closed while suspended. Email is the only thing that identifies a neighbor. The shed manager sees both accounts on the Neighbors screen and can suspend the new one.
    • The same rule applies when a neighbor changes their email (INV-CEM-2, Change Email).
  • INV-REG-5: Signing up has no approval or verification step.
    • Neighbor Registered is recorded straight from the request. Nothing waits for the shed manager, and the email address isn't confirmed first. The new neighbor can borrow straight away, under Check Out Tool's usual rules.
  • INV-REG-6: A neighbor whose account is closed may sign up again, and doing so creates a new account.
    • The new account has its own neighbor ID. The closed account stays closed; it is never reopened.
  • INV-REG-7: Registering with a neighbor ID that is already used adds nothing new.
    • A repeat with the same name and email, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the account since. A repeat with different details is refused (neighbor-id-in-use).
  • INV-REG-8: Each account gets its own neighbor ID when it registers, and keeps it for good.
    • The neighbor ID is how every later event, view and command refers to the account. Names and emails are for people to read and for the shed to send email to.
  • INV-REG-9: Neighbor names need not be unique.
    • Two neighbors may both be called "Sam Lee". Accounts are told apart by neighbor ID, and only the email is checked for uniqueness.
  • INV-REG-10: A name is at most 100 characters, and an email at most 254, counted as user-visible characters after trimming.
    • A longer one is refused, never cut short.
  • INV-REG-11: An email must be shaped like an email address: an "@" with at least one character before it and at least one after it.
    • Nothing more is checked; the address isn't confirmed by sending to it (INV-REG-5).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-REG-3, INV-REG-5, INV-REG-8)
    • Given: no account uses the email address ana@example.org
    • When: Ana signs up from the Sign Up screen as neighbor N1, with the name "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and the time it was recorded. Nothing waits for approval or email confirmation.
  • Whitespace is removed (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org
    • When: Ana signs up with the name " Ana Ruiz " and the email " ana@example.org "
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded with "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org.
  • No name (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up with ana@example.org and a name that is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with name-missing: "Please enter your name." No event is recorded.
  • No email (INV-REG-3)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up as "Ana Ruiz" with an email that is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with email-missing: "Please enter your email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by an active account (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N2 with ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used to sign up." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by a suspended account (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2 uses ben@example.org and is suspended
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N3 with ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used to sign up." No event is recorded.
  • Signing up again after closing (INV-REG-4, INV-REG-6, INV-REG-8)
    • Given: Ana's account N1, using ana@example.org, was closed while active
    • When: Ana signs up as N4 with "Ana Ruiz" and ana@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N4, a new account with its own neighbor ID. N1 keeps its neighbor ID and stays closed.
  • Email of an account closed while suspended (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N5 with ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used to sign up." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended, reinstated, then closed (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was suspended, then reinstated, and then closed while active
    • When: Ben signs up as N9 with ben@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N9. N2's Neighbor Account Closed has whileSuspended no, so its email is free again.
  • Different email after closing while suspended (INV-REG-4, INV-REG-6)
    • Given: Ben's account N2, using ben@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: Ben signs up as N5 with ben.new@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N5, a new account with its own neighbor ID. N2 stays closed.
  • Email an account has changed away from (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 registered with ana@oldmail.example and has since changed its email to ana@example.org
    • When: someone signs up as N6 with ana@oldmail.example
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N6. No account holds ana@oldmail.example any more.
  • Two neighbors with the same name (INV-REG-9)
    • Given: Sam Lee's account N7 uses sam@example.org
    • When: another person signs up as N8, also named "Sam Lee", with sam.lee@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N8. There are two accounts named "Sam Lee".
  • Email that differs only in capital letters (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: Ana's active account N1 uses ana@example.org
    • When: someone tries to sign up as N10 with Ana@Example.ORG
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used to sign up." No event is recorded.
  • Email kept as typed (INV-REG-4)
    • Given: no account uses ana@example.org in any case
    • When: Ana signs up as N1 with Ana@Example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded with Ana@Example.org.
  • Email not shaped like an address (INV-REG-11)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up as "Ana Ruiz" with ana.example.org
    • Then: refused with email-invalid: "Please enter a valid email address." No event is recorded.
  • Nothing before the "@" (INV-REG-11)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up with @example.org
    • Then: refused with email-invalid: "Please enter a valid email address." No event is recorded.
  • Longest name allowed (INV-REG-10)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone signs up with a name of exactly 100 characters
    • Then: Neighbor Registered is recorded with that name.
  • Name too long (INV-REG-10)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up with a name of 101 characters
    • Then: refused with name-too-long: "Your name can be at most 100 characters." No event is recorded.
  • Email too long (INV-REG-10)
    • Given: the shed has no neighbors
    • When: someone tries to sign up with an email of 255 characters
    • Then: refused with email-too-long: "Your email address can be at most 254 characters." No event is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • When: the same Register Neighbor request for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • The same request after the account was closed (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, and N1 has since been closed
    • When: the same Register Neighbor request for N1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. N1 stays closed.
  • A neighbor ID reused for different details (INV-REG-7)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • When: a Register Neighbor request arrives for N1 with "Ben Cole" and ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with neighbor-id-in-use: "That neighbor ID is already used by another account." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the person on the Sign Up screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. The neighbor ID is already used (INV-REG-7): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise neighbor-id-in-use.
  2. name-missing, then name-too-long (INV-REG-3, INV-REG-10).
  3. email-missing, then email-too-long, then email-invalid (INV-REG-3, INV-REG-10, INV-REG-11).
  4. email-in-use (INV-REG-4).
Reason Sentence Rule
name-missing Please enter your name. INV-REG-3
name-too-long Your name can be at most 100 characters. INV-REG-10
email-missing Please enter your email address. INV-REG-3
email-too-long Your email address can be at most 254 characters. INV-REG-10
email-invalid Please enter a valid email address. INV-REG-11
email-in-use That email address can't be used to sign up. INV-REG-4
neighbor-id-in-use That neighbor ID is already used by another account. INV-REG-7

email-in-use is the same for every case in INV-REG-4, with a sentence that is true in each, so a refused sign-up never reveals whether the other account is active, suspended, or closed while suspended.

neighbor-id-in-use can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen.

A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same neighbor ID and the same name and email, compared after trimming and with the email compared ignoring case, succeeds and records nothing new, even if the account has since been suspended, closed, or had its email changed. So a retry after a lost response never creates a second account. The repeat is recognised by its neighbor ID, and is checked before the email rule, so it is never refused as email-in-use by its own earlier registration.

Two sign-ups with the same email at the same moment: the email check and the recording of Neighbor Registered happen as one step, so at most one is recorded. The other is refused with email-in-use.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice. No email is sent on sign-up.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: anyone may sign up; signing up needs no existing account or sign-in. Afterwards, sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID for their own actions.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Registered holds the neighbor's name and email address. It is read by the shed manager's screens (Neighbors, Tool Inventory, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors, Suspended Neighbors), by the neighbor's own My Account, and by the two email to-do lists. No neighbor-facing screen shows another neighbor's name: the Tool Catalog never shows who has or holds a tool. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased, including a closed account's; there is no erasure on request.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply INV-REG-4 and INV-REG-7, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (this slice): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId, whileSuspended.
    • Neighbor Email Changed matches slices/change-email.md. Close Account is specified in a slice being written in depth; it is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Neighbors and My Account (a new entry); Tool Inventory, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the neighbor's name and email). Every later neighbor action (check out, hold, extend, return, change email, close account) and every shed-manager action on a neighbor refers to the account by its neighbor ID.

Open Questions

None.

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v1: v1 keeps the old view names in prose; the views named no longer exist in the model; deferred to v2 (2026-11-01, Mike Key)
"},{"index":2,"name":"Tool Inventory — neighbor registered","x0":458.76,"x1":602.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Tool Inventory

Intent

Shows the shed manager every tool in the shed on the Tool Inventory screen, and which of them are out on loan, to whom, and until when. It is the shed manager's working screen for tools: they add and retire tools from it, and record a tool lost when it is out and never coming back.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Tool Inventory screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per tool currently in the shed or out on loan, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Add Tool (Add Tool slice) — always offered.
    • Retire (Retire Tool slice) — offered on every listed tool that is not already retired (INV-TINV-7).
    • Mark lost (Record Tool Lost slice) — offered only on a tool that is out on loan (INV-TINV-6).

Read Model / View

  • View: Tool Inventory built from events: "Tool Added", "Neighbor Registered", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost"
  • Consumed by: the Tool Inventory screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual — an entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because each command checks its own rules when it runs.

One row per listed tool. ToolId, NeighborId and LoanId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

Field Type Source / Notes
toolId ToolId Tool Added.toolId.
name Text Tool Added.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
description Text Optional: absent when the tool was added without one. Tool Added.description.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int Tool Added.defaultCheckoutPeriodDays (1–30).
addedAt Instant Tool Added.addedAt.
onLoan Bool Derived: yes from Tool Checked Out for this tool until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan; no otherwise.
loanId LoanId Derived: Tool Checked Out.loanId while the tool is on loan; none once Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan lands. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerId NeighborId Derived: Tool Checked Out.neighborId while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
borrowerName Text Derived: Neighbor Registered.name for borrowerId while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
dueDate Date Derived: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for that loan, while the tool is on loan; none otherwise. Optional: present only while on loan.
retired Bool Derived: yes once Tool Retired is recorded for this tool. A retired row exists only while the tool is still out on loan.
canRetire Bool Derived: yes while retired is no. Returned so the screen can offer Retire (INV-TINV-7).
overdue Bool Derived: yes while the tool is on loan and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after dueDate; no otherwise (INV-TINV-9). Worked out when the inventory is read.
canMarkLost Bool Derived: same as onLoan. Returned so the screen can offer Mark lost (INV-TINV-6).

Queries

  • List the tool inventory. Takes nothing. Returns every listed tool, each with all the fields above. There is no paging: the query always returns every listed tool. Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added (addedAt); tools added at the same instant keep the order their Tool Added was recorded (INV-TINV-10).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-TINV-1: Every added tool appears in the inventory exactly once.
    • One entry per Tool Added; nothing else creates an entry.
    • Each physical item is its own tool, so two identical drills are two entries.
  • INV-TINV-2: A retired tool drops off the inventory once it is back in the shed or recorded lost.
    • A tool retired while it is in the shed drops off at once.
    • A tool retired while it is out on loan stays listed, marked retired and out, until it is returned or recorded lost. Then it drops off. This lets the shed manager record it lost if it never comes back.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it drops off too.
    • This differs from the Tool Catalog, where a tool retired while on loan drops off at once: neighbors can do nothing with it, while the shed manager may still need to record it lost.
  • INV-TINV-3: The inventory changes only when a tool is added, checked out, extended, returned, retired or recorded lost, or when a neighbor registers.
    • Neighbor Registered supplies the borrower names shown on tools that are out.
    • Holds and overdue notices leave it unchanged. Hold state is shown to neighbors on the Tool Catalog, not here.
    • A tool's details never change after it is added (see the note under Add Tool's event table). A mistake is corrected by retiring the tool and adding it again.
  • INV-TINV-4: Each entry shows the tool's name, its description when it has one, and its default checkout period.
  • INV-TINV-5: Each entry shows whether the tool is out on loan. A tool that is out also shows the borrower's name and the due date.
    • A tool is out from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost.
    • The due date moves with each extension.
    • When the tool comes back or is recorded lost, the borrower's name and due date are no longer shown on it.
  • INV-TINV-6: The inventory offers "mark lost" only on a tool that is out on loan.
    • Recording a tool lost ends its loan, retires the tool and ends its holds. It never counts as a late return for the borrower (Record Tool Lost).
  • INV-TINV-7: The inventory offers "retire" on every listed tool that is not already retired.
    • A tool retired while out on loan stays listed but is not offered "retire" again.
  • INV-TINV-8: Applying the same event twice leaves the inventory as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-TINV-9: A tool that is out shows whether its loan is overdue.
    • Overdue means today's date in the shed's local time zone is after the due date in force. It is worked out when the inventory is read; no event marks a loan overdue.
  • INV-TINV-10: Tools are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they were added.
    • Tools with the same name are in the order they were added; tools added at the same instant keep the order their Tool Added was recorded.
  • INV-TINV-11: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-TINV-12: Only the shed manager can read the Tool Inventory: a caller signed in without the shed-manager role is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Tool added (INV-TINV-1, INV-TINV-4, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a cordless drill, described as "18V, two batteries", with a default checkout period of 7 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill with its description and its 7-day default checkout period, in the shed, with "retire" offered and no "mark lost".
  • Tool added without a description (INV-TINV-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a ladder with no description and a default checkout period of 3 days
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists the ladder with its 3-day default checkout period and no description.
  • Two of the same tool (INV-TINV-1)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists one cordless drill
    • When: Tool Added is recorded for a second cordless drill, with its own tool ID
    • Then: the Tool Inventory lists both drills as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-TINV-8)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill once
    • When: the same Tool Added for that drill is applied again
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the drill once.
  • Neighbor registers (INV-TINV-3)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the drill, in the shed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for Ana Ruiz
    • Then: no entry on the Tool Inventory changes.
  • Tool checked out (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: Neighbor Registered was recorded for Ana Ruiz, and the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill, in the shed
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for Ana borrowing the drill, due 12 October
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as out on loan to Ana Ruiz, the name she registered with, due 12 October, and offers "mark lost" on it.
  • Loan extended (INV-TINV-5)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Loan Extended is recorded for Ana's drill loan, with the due date 19 October
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October.
  • Tool returned (INV-TINV-5, INV-TINV-6)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 19 October
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the Tool Inventory shows the drill as in the shed, with no borrower, due date or "mark lost".
  • Tool retired (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists a cordless drill and a ladder, both in the shed
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: the cordless drill drops off the Tool Inventory, and the ladder is still listed.
  • Tool retired while out on loan (INV-TINV-2, INV-TINV-6, INV-TINV-7)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder out on loan to Ben, due 20 October
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the ladder
    • Then: the Tool Inventory still lists the ladder, marked retired and out on loan to Ben, due 20 October, with "mark lost" still offered and "retire" no longer offered.
  • Retired tool comes back (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Retired tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the ladder marked retired and out on loan to Ben
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ben's ladder loan
    • Then: the ladder drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-TINV-2)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the hedge trimmer out on loan to Ana
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for Ana's hedge trimmer loan
    • Then: the hedge trimmer drops off the Tool Inventory.
  • Out tool becomes overdue (INV-TINV-9)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: the inventory is read at 23:59 on 12 October, and again at 00:00 on 13 October, shed time
    • Then: the drill shows not overdue on the first read and overdue on the second. Nothing is recorded.
  • List order (INV-TINV-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for "Ladder", then "Cordless drill", then a second "Cordless drill"
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: the order is the first "Cordless drill", the second "Cordless drill", then "Ladder".
  • Holds and notices don't change it (INV-TINV-3)
    • Given: the Tool Inventory shows the drill out on loan to Ana, due 12 October
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben on the drill, and later Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for Ana's drill loan
    • Then: the drill's entry is unchanged.
  • Listing the inventory
    • Given: the Tool Inventory lists the cordless drill (in the shed) and the ladder (out on loan to Ben, due 20 October)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the tool inventory
    • Then: both tools are returned with all their fields, with no paging.
  • Not signed in (INV-TINV-11)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: the tool inventory is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-TINV-12)
    • Given: a neighbor is signed in, without the shed-manager role
    • When: the tool inventory is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see the tool inventory." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-TINV-11).
  2. not-shed-manager (INV-TINV-12).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-TINV-11
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can see the tool inventory. INV-TINV-12
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-TINV-8). A Tool Added, Tool Checked Out, Loan Extended, Tool Returned, Tool Retired or Tool Lost applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for a tool that is no longer listed: under the rules above, a Loan Extended, Tool Returned or Tool Lost can reach this view for a tool that is no longer listed only as a replay of an event already applied. It changes nothing.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, "mark lost" on a tool that has just been returned). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Tool Inventory is the shed manager's screen; neighbors see tools on the Tool Catalog instead. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the shed-manager role; a caller without it is refused not-shed-manager (INV-TINV-12), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-TINV-11).
  • PII & compliance: shows a borrower's name while they have a tool out. It never shows their email. The name stops being shown on that tool once the loan ends.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name, description, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays, addedAt.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId.
    • All but Tool Added are specified in slices not yet written in depth. These names are this view's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Add Tool, Retire Tool and Record Tool Lost.

Open Questions

None.
