Slice: Neighbors

Intent

Shows the shed manager every neighbor account that has signed up, with each account's current status (active, suspended or closed), on the Neighbors screen. It is the shed manager's one screen for neighbors: it shows who the system has flagged for repeated late returns and the late returns behind each flag, who is suspended and since when, and account closures, and it is the screen the shed manager suspends and reinstates neighbors from. The system flags; the shed manager decides.

Version 2 folds the former Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors views into this one: both were filters of the same accounts, and each offered one action this screen now offers.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Neighbors screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per account ever registered, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Suspend (Suspend Neighbor slice) — offered on every active account, flagged or not (INV-NBRS-6).
    • Reinstate (Reinstate Neighbor slice) — offered on every suspended account (INV-NBRS-13).
  • Flagging is done by the system (Flag Neighbor). A neighbor is not told they were flagged, and a suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag, INV-NTF-7). No email goes to the neighbor on suspension or reinstatement, and no reason or note is recorded with a suspension.
  • Showing only the flagged accounts, or only the suspended ones, is the screen's own filter over this one list; there is no separate read model for either.

Read Model / View

  • View: Neighbors built from events: "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Neighbor Flagged", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed", and, to name the late returns behind a flag, "Tool Added", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned"
  • Consumed by: the Neighbors screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Suspend and Reinstate check their own rules when they run, so a stale entry can't suspend someone who is no longer active or reinstate someone who is no longer suspended.

One row per account. NeighborId, LoanId and ToolId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Neighbor Registered.neighborId.
name Text Neighbor Registered.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
email Text Neighbor Registered.email, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for this account. Always the account's current email.
registeredAt Instant Neighbor Registered.registeredAt. Shown as the sign-up date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone (INV-NBRS-5).
status Text One of active, suspended, closed. Derived: see the status rules below.
suspendedAt Instant Derived: suspendedAt of the Neighbor Suspended behind a suspended status; empty otherwise (INV-NBRS-12). Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.
flagCount Int Derived: the number of open flags on the account: Neighbor Flagged recorded since the account was last suspended, or ever if never suspended (INV-NBRS-10, INV-NBRS-11). 0 when the account is not flagged.
latestFlaggedAt Instant Derived: flaggedAt of the latest open flag; empty when flagCount is 0. Shown as a date in the shed's local time zone.
lateReturns LateReturn[] Derived: one item for each loan named by the account's open flags, as below; empty when flagCount is 0.
canSuspend Bool Derived: yes while status is active (INV-NBRS-6).
canReinstate Bool Derived: yes while status is suspended (INV-NBRS-13).

Each LateReturn item:

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId One of Neighbor Flagged.loanIds.
toolName Text Tool Added.name for the loan's tool (Tool Checked Out.toolId).
dueDate Date The loan's due date in force when it was returned: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for the loan.
returnedOn Date Tool Returned.returnedOn for the loan.
flaggedAt Instant flaggedAt of the Neighbor Flagged that named this loan.

To fill the late returns when a flag lands, the view also keeps, beyond its rows: every tool's name and, for every loan, its tool, current due date and return date. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned (INV-NBRS-14).

Status rules. An account's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. closed — Neighbor Account Closed has been recorded for the account.
  2. suspended — otherwise, Neighbor Suspended has been recorded and no Neighbor Reinstated since.
  3. active — otherwise.

Flag rules. A flag is open from its Neighbor Flagged until the account is next suspended or closed; suspension and closure clear the account's open flags (INV-NBRS-11). A Neighbor Flagged recorded after a reinstatement starts the account's flags afresh.

Queries

  • List the neighbors. Takes nothing. Returns every account, each with every field above, including its late returns. There is no paging: the query always returns every account, ordered by name, then by registeredAt (INV-NBRS-8). The screen filters to flagged (flagCount above 0) or suspended accounts itself.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-NBRS-1: Every account appears on the Neighbors screen exactly once.
    • One entry per Neighbor Registered; nothing else creates an entry. A neighbor who signs up again after closing their account has a new account, so they appear twice: the closed entry and the new one.
  • INV-NBRS-2: Each account's status is active, suspended or closed, worked out by the status rules above.
    • Neighbor Registered → active. Neighbor Suspended → suspended. Neighbor Reinstated → active. Neighbor Account Closed → closed.
  • INV-NBRS-3: An account that is closed stays listed, shown as closed.
    • This screen is where the shed manager sees account closures. It is the record of every account; a closed account keeps its row, with no action offered and no open flags.
  • INV-NBRS-4: Closed is final.
    • A suspended neighbor who closes their account shows as closed, not suspended. No later event changes a closed account's status.
  • INV-NBRS-5: Each entry shows the account's name, its current email, its sign-up date, and its status.
    • The email is set by Neighbor Registered and replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed. The name never changes.
  • INV-NBRS-6: The screen offers Suspend on every active account, whether or not the neighbor has been flagged, and on no other.
    • Suspend Neighbor checks its own rules when it runs.
  • INV-NBRS-8: Accounts are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they signed up.
    • So a neighbor who signed up again after closing appears twice, the older account first.
  • INV-NBRS-7: Applying the same event twice leaves the Neighbors screen as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-NBRS-9: Only the shed manager can read the Neighbors screen.
    • A signed-in caller without the shed-manager role is refused with not-shed-manager, and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned to either.
  • INV-NBRS-10: A flagged account shows how many open flags it has, the date of the latest, and the late returns behind every open flag, each with the tool's name, its due date, the date it was returned, and the date of the flag that named it.
    • Neighbor Flagged names the late returns it uses up, as the loans they belong to. It carries no copies of names or dates. The view looks those loans up in the loan events it hears: the tool from Tool Checked Out and its name from Tool Added, the due date from Tool Checked Out as moved by any Loan Extended, and the return date from Tool Returned.
    • Being flagged never suspends anyone by itself, and there is no dismiss action: a flag the shed manager decides not to act on stays open.
  • INV-NBRS-11: Suspending or closing the account clears its open flags; a flag recorded after a reinstatement starts the count afresh.
    • The flags were what the shed manager acted on, or can no longer act on. A suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag), so no flag lands while suspended.
  • INV-NBRS-12: A suspended account shows when it was suspended; the date is cleared on reinstatement.
    • A suspension never lifts by itself after a set time, and it is never permanent. A neighbor suspended again after a reinstatement shows the new date.
  • INV-NBRS-13: The screen offers Reinstate on every suspended account, and on no other.
    • Reinstate Neighbor checks its own rules when it runs.
  • INV-NBRS-14: To name late returns, the view keeps every tool's name and every loan's tool, current due date and return date, whether or not the borrower is flagged; none of it is returned on its own.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org and Ben Ito with ben@example.org. Ana returned the ladder (L1, due 31 August) on 1 September, the drill (L2, due 15 September) on 20 September and the hedge trimmer (L3, due 1 October) on 5 October, all late.

  • Neighbor registered (INV-NBRS-1, INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-5, INV-NBRS-6)
    • Given: no neighbors have signed up
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, signed up on today's date, as active, not flagged, with Suspend offered and Reinstate not offered.
  • Two neighbors with the same name (INV-NBRS-1)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a different account, also named Ana Ruiz, with ana.r@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists both, as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-NBRS-7)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana once, as active
    • When: the same Neighbor Registered for Ana is applied again
    • Then: the Neighbors screen still lists Ana once.
  • Email changed (INV-NBRS-5)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz with ana@example.org, as active
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz with ana.ruiz@example.net, still active.
  • Neighbor flagged (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana as active, not flagged
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 5 October, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active, flagged once, latest on 5 October, with three late returns: the ladder (due 31 August, returned 1 September), the drill (due 15 September, returned 20 September) and the hedge trimmer (due 1 October, returned 5 October). Suspend is offered, as before.
  • Due date after an extension (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: L2 was extended from 15 September to 18 September before it was returned on 20 September
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the drill's late return shows due 18 September, returned 20 September.
  • Flagged again (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged once on 5 October, and she has since returned three more tools late (L4, L5, L6)
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 15 November, naming L4, L5 and L6
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged twice, latest on 15 November, with all six late returns: L1, L2 and L3 flagged 5 October, and L4, L5 and L6 flagged 15 November.
  • Flag left alone (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has shown Ana flagged since 5 October, and the shed manager has not suspended her
    • When: a month passes with no Neighbor Suspended recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana is still shown flagged once, with the same late returns.
  • Flagged neighbor changes their email (INV-NBRS-5, INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, flagged once
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz, ana.ruiz@example.net. Her flags are unchanged.
  • Neighbor suspended (INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-11, INV-NBRS-12, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active, flagged once, and Ben as active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana on 7 October
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 7 October, with no open flags, Suspend not offered and Reinstate offered. Ben is unchanged.
  • Suspended without a flag (INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-12)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ben as active, not flagged
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ben on 9 October
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ben as suspended since 9 October, with Reinstate offered.
  • Neighbor reinstated (INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-12, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 7 October
    • When: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active again, with no suspended date, not flagged, with Suspend offered and Reinstate not offered.
  • Flagged again after reinstatement (INV-NBRS-11)
    • Given: Ana was flagged, then suspended, which cleared her flags, and later reinstated
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 20 January, naming L7, L8 and L9
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged once, latest on 20 January, with only L7, L8 and L9.
  • Suspended again after reinstatement (INV-NBRS-12)
    • Given: Ana was suspended on 7 October and reinstated on 1 November
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana again on 3 February
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 3 February.
  • Account closed (INV-NBRS-3, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-11)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana as active, flagged once
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen still lists Ana, now shown as closed, with no open flags and neither Suspend nor Reinstate offered.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-NBRS-4, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as closed, with Reinstate not offered.
  • Closed stays closed (INV-NBRS-4)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana's account as closed
    • When: an earlier Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated or Neighbor Flagged for that account is applied again
    • Then: the account is still shown as closed, with no open flags.
  • Signing up again after closing (INV-NBRS-1, INV-NBRS-3)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz's account, ana@example.org, as closed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a new account for Ana Ruiz, with ana@example.org
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists two entries for Ana Ruiz with ana@example.org: the old account, still closed, and the new one, active, with Suspend offered.
  • Listing order (INV-NBRS-8)
    • Given: Ben Ito signed up on 2 October; Ana Ruiz signed up on 1 October, closed her account, and signed up again on 5 October
    • When: the shed manager lists the neighbors
    • Then: the accounts come back as: Ana Ruiz (signed up 1 October, closed), Ana Ruiz (signed up 5 October, active), then Ben Ito.
  • Listing the neighbors
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana (active, flagged once), Ben (suspended) and Cara (closed)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the neighbors
    • Then: all three are returned with all their fields, Ana's with her late returns, with no paging. Only Ana's entry offers Suspend; only Ben's offers Reinstate.
  • A neighbor tries to read the list (INV-NBRS-9)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has entries
    • When: a neighbor, signed in without the shed-manager role, asks for the neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see this screen." Nothing is returned.
  • No sign-in (INV-NBRS-9)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has entries
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller without the shed-manager role with not-shed-manager ("Only the shed manager can see this screen."), and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal. These mean the same conditions as in the shed manager's commands.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-NBRS-7). An event applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for an account the view hasn't seen: events are applied in the order they were recorded, and every account starts with Neighbor Registered, so this can't happen.
  • Events on a closed account: a Neighbor Flagged, Neighbor Suspended or Neighbor Reinstated applied to a closed account changes nothing (INV-NBRS-4).
  • Stale actions: Suspend or Reinstate offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, on a neighbor who has just closed their account). Suspend Neighbor and Reinstate Neighbor check their own rules and refuse with their own reasons; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Neighbors screen is the shed manager's alone; neighbors see only their own account, on My Account. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; only a caller with it may read this view.
  • PII & compliance: shows every account's name, current email, sign-up date, status, suspension date and late-return history to the shed manager, including closed accounts, which stay listed. A replaced email is not kept in the view. To name late returns, the view keeps every tool's name and every loan's tool and dates, whether or not the borrower is flagged. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and are never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email, registeredAt.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Flagged (Flag Neighbor): neighborId, loanIds (LoanId[]), flaggedAt.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId, suspendedAt.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, returnedOn.
    • These keys match slices/register-neighbor.md, flag-neighbor.md, suspend-neighbor.md and the loan slices' docs.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Suspend Neighbor and Reinstate Neighbor.
  • Lineage: v2 merges Flagged Neighbors v1 and Suspended Neighbors v1 into this view (model reshape, 2026-11-01). Their docs stay in slices/ marked superseded by neighbors@v2.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":4,"name":"My Account","x0":796.76,"x1":940.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: My Account

Intent

Shows a neighbor their own account on the My Account screen: their name, their current email, and whether the account is active, suspended or closed. It is where a neighbor learns they are suspended, and the screen they change their email and close their account from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Account screen. A neighbor whose account is closed can still open it, read-only.
  • Whose account it shows: the account of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Change Email (Change Email slice) — offered while the account isn't closed (INV-MYAC-9).
    • Close Account (Close Account slice) — offered while the account isn't closed (INV-MYAC-11).

Read Model / View

  • View: My Account built from events: "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the My Account screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. A change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because Change Email and Close Account each check their own rules when they run.

One row per account. A NeighborId is a UUID. An Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Neighbor Registered.neighborId.
name Text Neighbor Registered.name. Never changes.
email Text Neighbor Registered.email, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for this account. Always the current one.
status Text One of active, suspended, closed. Derived: see the status rules below.
canChangeEmail Bool Derived: yes unless status is closed (INV-MYAC-9).
canCloseAccount Bool Derived: yes unless status is closed (INV-MYAC-11).

My Account doesn't show the neighbor's sign-up date; that is the shed manager's to see, on Neighbors.

Status rules. An account's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. closed — Neighbor Account Closed has been recorded for the account. Closed is final.
  2. suspended — otherwise, Neighbor Suspended has been recorded and no Neighbor Reinstated since.
  3. active — otherwise.

Queries

  • Get my account. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns that one account with every field above, or not found if no account has that neighbor ID. It never returns another account (INV-MYAC-1).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-MYAC-1: A neighbor's My Account shows only their own account.
    • The query returns the one account whose neighbor ID it is given, and nothing about any other account.
  • INV-MYAC-2: My Account shows the neighbor's name and their current email.
    • Neighbor Registered sets the email. Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The name never changes after sign-up.
  • INV-MYAC-3: A newly registered neighbor's account shows as active.
    • One account per Neighbor Registered.
  • INV-MYAC-4: A suspended neighbor's account shows as suspended until they are reinstated, and then shows as active again.
    • This is how a neighbor learns they are suspended; they aren't emailed about it.
  • INV-MYAC-5: Once a neighbor closes their account, it shows as closed, permanently.
    • Closed is final. A suspended neighbor who closes their account sees it as closed, not suspended.
  • INV-MYAC-6: After closing their account, the neighbor can still view My Account, read-only.
    • Close Account and Change Email are no longer offered on a closed account.
  • INV-MYAC-7: Only Neighbor Registered, Neighbor Email Changed, Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated and Neighbor Account Closed change My Account.
    • Loans, holds and flags never change it.
  • INV-MYAC-8: A person who signs up again after closing an account has a new account, and My Account shows them only that new account.
    • Each account has its own neighbor ID, and the query returns the one account it is asked for. The old, closed account is no longer shown to them. It stays on the shed manager's Neighbors screen.
  • INV-MYAC-9: My Account offers Change Email on any account that isn't closed.
    • It is offered to a suspended neighbor too. Change Email refuses them with its own reason (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email), and they can change it once reinstated. A refusal with a reason they see means the action was offered.
  • INV-MYAC-10: Applying the same event twice leaves My Account as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYAC-11: My Account offers Close Account on any account that isn't closed.
    • It is offered whether or not the neighbor has tools on loan. Close Account refuses a neighbor with tools on loan with its own reason (INV-CLS-7, Close Account): a refusal with a reason the neighbor sees means the action was offered.
  • INV-MYAC-13: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYAC-14: My Account is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Neighbor registered (INV-MYAC-2, INV-MYAC-3, INV-MYAC-9, INV-MYAC-11)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N1
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N1, with the name "Ana Ruiz" and the email ana@example.org
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active, with Change Email and Close Account offered.
  • Email changed (INV-MYAC-2)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana.ruiz@example.net, active.
  • Neighbor suspended (INV-MYAC-4, INV-MYAC-9, INV-MYAC-11)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows suspended. Change Email and Close Account are still offered.
  • Neighbor reinstated (INV-MYAC-4)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows suspended
    • When: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows active.
  • Email changed after reinstatement (INV-MYAC-2, INV-MYAC-4)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and then reinstated, and My Account for N1 shows ana@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows ana.ruiz@example.net, active.
  • Account closed (INV-MYAC-5, INV-MYAC-6)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows closed, with neither Change Email nor Close Account offered. It can still be read.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-MYAC-5)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows suspended
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows closed, not suspended.
  • Signed up again after closing (INV-MYAC-8)
    • Given: account N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, is closed, and was not suspended when it was closed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a new account N4, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • Then: My Account for N4 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active. My Account for N1 still shows closed; asking for N4 never returns N1.
  • Only their own account (INV-MYAC-1)
    • Given: accounts N1 (Ana) and N2 (Ben) are both registered
    • When: My Account is asked for N1
    • Then: it returns Ana's account only. Nothing about Ben's account is returned.
  • Another neighbor's change (INV-MYAC-1, INV-MYAC-7)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N2
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged.
  • Loans and holds don't change it (INV-MYAC-7)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for N1, and later Hold Placed for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYAC-10)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: the same Neighbor Registered for N1 is applied again
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged, and there is still one account N1.
  • Asking for an account that doesn't exist (INV-MYAC-1)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: My Account is asked for N9
    • Then: not found.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYAC-13)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Account is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYAC-14)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: My Account is asked for N1, Ana's account
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own account." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYAC-13).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYAC-14).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-MYAC-13
requester-mismatch You can only see your own account. INV-MYAC-14
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYAC-10). An event applied a second time leaves the account as it was after the first.
  • Events for a closed account: closed is final, so no Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated or Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for a closed account (Close Account: nothing reopens, suspends or reinstates a closed account; Change Email, INV-CEM-3). If one reaches this view, it can only be a replay, and it changes nothing.
  • Unknown neighbor ID: the query returns not found. The screen shows that no account was found rather than an error.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Change Email just after the neighbor was suspended). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may read only their own account (INV-MYAC-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYAC-14), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYAC-13).
  • PII & compliance: holds and shows the neighbor's name and email, to that neighbor only. Names and emails are kept with the shed's history and never erased, including a closed account's.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Change Email, Suspend Neighbor, Reinstate Neighbor and Close Account aren't yet written in depth. These names are this view's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Change Email and Close Account.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":5,"name":"Change Email","x0":965.76,"x1":1109.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Change Email

Intent

Let a neighbor change the email address the shed uses for them, from My Account, so a wrong or outdated address can be put right and overdue and pickup emails reach them. The new address takes effect at once, and the old one is free for anyone to use.

Trigger & Actor

A neighbor, from their own My Account screen, for their own account. My Account offers Change Email on any account that isn't closed (INV-MYAC-9); a suspended neighbor is offered it and refused with a reason they can see. The shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails.

Command / Input

Command: Change Email

A NeighborId is a UUID. Text has leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed; text that is empty after that counts as absent.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
neighborId NeighborId yes The account whose email changes, which must be the neighbor making the request (INV-CEM-1) and a registered account (INV-CEM-10).
email Text yes The new email. Trimmed; must not then be empty (INV-CEM-11), at most 254 characters, and shaped like an email address (INV-CEM-12). Must not be held by another account under INV-CEM-2, compared ignoring case. Kept as typed.

There is no name field: only the email can be changed. A neighbor's name stays as they registered it.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen My Account @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Neighbor Email Changed → context Neighbors Read by: My Account and Neighbors (the email shown); Overdue Loans To Notify and Pickup Notices To Send (the address the next email goes to); Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the email shown to the shed manager).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command.
email Text yes From the command, trimmed. The account's current email from now on.
changedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

The event never changes. A later change records a new Neighbor Email Changed. An account's current email is the email of its latest Neighbor Email Changed, or of its Neighbor Registered if it has never changed it.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Neighbor Email Changed updates the email in My Account, Neighbors, Overdue Loans To Notify, Pickup Notices To Send, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors, each specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent: the new email shows once each has caught up. Every overdue or pickup email the shed sends from then on, including one for a loan or set-aside already waiting to be emailed, goes to the new address.

Invariants / Business Rules

Changing the email resends nothing. A notice already sent, or already recorded as undelivered, is not tried again at the new address: no further attempt is made after a failure (Record Overdue Notice Failure, INV-ONF-6).

  • INV-CEM-1: A neighbor changes their own email themselves, from My Account.
    • The request must come from the neighbor whose account it names. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch. The shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails.
  • INV-CEM-2: The new email is refused if it belongs to an account that is not closed, or to a closed account that was suspended when it was closed.
    • This is the same one-account-per-email rule as at sign-up (INV-REG-4, Register Neighbor). An account's email is always its current one.
    • Emails are compared ignoring case. The account's own current email never counts as held by another account.
    • Whether a closed account was suspended when it was closed is read from its Neighbor Account Closed (whileSuspended), never worked out from earlier suspensions and reinstatements.
  • INV-CEM-3: A neighbor whose account is closed can't change their email.
    • After closing, My Account is read-only.
  • INV-CEM-3a: A suspended neighbor can't change their email. The change is refused with a reason they can see, and they can change it once reinstated.
    • Otherwise a suspended neighbor could change to a new address, close their account, and sign up again with their original address.
  • INV-CEM-4: Once changed, the account's email is the new one.
    • Every later check of INV-CEM-2 and INV-REG-4 treats the new email as held by this account.
  • INV-CEM-5: The old email is released.
    • No account holds it any more, so it can be used to sign up or by another neighbor's change.
  • INV-CEM-7: The new email takes effect at once, with no verification.
    • Neighbor Email Changed is recorded straight from the request; nothing is sent to the new address first.
  • INV-CEM-9: Asking to change the email to the one the account already has succeeds and records nothing.
    • The comparison is made after trimming, exactly as typed. So a repeated request, after a lost response, never records a second change. A request that differs from the current email only in capital letters is a change, and is recorded: it is how a neighbor corrects the capitalisation of their address.
    • The command carries no "from" email. A late copy of an older request, arriving after a later change, counts as a new request and changes the email again.
  • INV-CEM-10: The neighbor must be a registered account.
  • INV-CEM-11: A new email is required.
    • An email that is empty, or only whitespace, is missing.
  • INV-CEM-12: A new email is at most 254 user-visible characters, counted after trimming, and must be shaped like an email address: an "@" with at least one character before it and at least one after it.
    • A longer one is refused, never cut short. These are the same limits as at sign-up (INV-REG-10, INV-REG-11, Register Neighbor).
  • INV-CEM-13: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path (INV-CEM-1, INV-CEM-4, INV-CEM-7)
    • Given: Ana's account N1 is active with ana@oldmail.example, and no other account uses ana@example.org
    • When: Ana changes her email to ana@example.org from My Account
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with ana@example.org and the time it was recorded. Nothing is sent to the new address first.
  • Whitespace is removed (INV-CEM-11)
    • Given: N1 is active with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Ana changes her email to " ana@example.org "
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded with ana@example.org.
  • Same email as now (INV-CEM-9)
    • Given: N1's current email is ana@example.org
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ana@example.org
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CEM-9)
    • Given: Neighbor Email Changed was recorded for N1, to ana@example.org
    • When: the same Change Email request for N1, ana@example.org, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • No email (INV-CEM-11)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to an empty value, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with email-missing: "Please enter your email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by an active account (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Ben's active account N2 uses ben@example.org
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ben@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Email used by a suspended account (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Cleo's account N3 uses cleo@example.org and is suspended
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to cleo@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Email of an account closed while suspended (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Dan's account N4, using dan@example.org, was closed while suspended
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to dan@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Email of an account closed while active (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Eve's account N5, using eve@example.org, was closed while active
    • When: Ana changes her email to eve@example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with eve@example.org.
  • Email held in different capitals (INV-CEM-2)
    • Given: Ben's active account N2 uses ben@example.org
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to Ben@Example.ORG
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Correcting capital letters (INV-CEM-2, INV-CEM-9)
    • Given: N1's current email is ana@example.org
    • When: Ana changes her email to Ana@Example.org
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with Ana@Example.org. Her own account doesn't count as holding the address.
  • Email not shaped like an address (INV-CEM-12)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ana.example.org
    • Then: refused with email-invalid: "Please enter a valid email address." No event is recorded.
  • Email too long (INV-CEM-12)
    • Given: N1 is active
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to an address of 255 characters
    • Then: refused with email-too-long: "Your email address can be at most 254 characters." No event is recorded.
  • Old email released (INV-CEM-5)
    • Given: Ana changed N1's email from ana@oldmail.example to ana@example.org
    • When: Ben asks to change N2's email to ana@oldmail.example
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N2, with ana@oldmail.example.
  • The new email is held from then on (INV-CEM-4)
    • Given: Ana changed N1's email to ana@example.org
    • When: Ben asks to change N2's email to ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with email-in-use: "That email address can't be used." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-CEM-3a)
    • Given: N1 is suspended, with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: Ana asks to change her email to ana@example.org
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't change your email while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Changing the email after reinstatement (INV-CEM-3a)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and has since been reinstated, and no other account uses ana.ruiz@example.org
    • When: Ana changes her email to ana.ruiz@example.org from My Account
    • Then: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, with ana.ruiz@example.org.
  • Closed account (INV-CEM-3)
    • Given: N1 is closed, with ana@oldmail.example
    • When: a change of N1's email to ana@example.org is requested
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • A request for someone else's account (INV-CEM-1)
    • Given: N1 and N2 are both active
    • When: a request from Ben asks to change N1's email
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only change your own email." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-CEM-10)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: a change of N9's email is requested
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Not signed in (INV-CEM-13)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: a request for changing an email arrives
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on My Account. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-CEM-13): a request with no sign-in is refused first.
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-CEM-1): who is asking is settled next, before any other rule.
  3. neighbor-not-found (INV-CEM-10).
  4. email-missing, then email-too-long, then email-invalid (INV-CEM-11, INV-CEM-12).
  5. The new email is the account's current one (INV-CEM-9): succeeds with nothing recorded.
  6. account-closed (INV-CEM-3).
  7. neighbor-suspended (INV-CEM-3a).
  8. email-in-use (INV-CEM-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-CEM-13
requester-mismatch You can only change your own email. INV-CEM-1
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-CEM-10
email-missing Please enter your email address. INV-CEM-11
account-closed This account is closed. INV-CEM-3
neighbor-suspended You can't change your email while your account is suspended. INV-CEM-3a
email-too-long Your email address can be at most 254 characters. INV-CEM-12
email-invalid Please enter a valid email address. INV-CEM-12
email-in-use That email address can't be used. INV-CEM-2

neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed neighbor ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. email-missing, email-too-long, email-invalid, email-in-use, account-closed and neighbor-not-found mean the same conditions as in Register Neighbor and Check Out Tool. email-in-use is one reason for every case of INV-CEM-2, worded to be true in each, so a refusal never reveals another account's status; its sentence fits a change rather than a sign-up.

Idempotency: there is no request ID. A request whose effect has already happened, because the account's current email is already the one asked for, succeeds and records nothing (INV-CEM-9).

Requests at the same moment: the email check and the recording of Neighbor Email Changed happen as one step, shared with Register Neighbor, so no two accounts are ever given the same email. Of two requests for the same email at once, from a sign-up or a change, at most one is recorded; the other is refused with email-in-use.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice. Nothing is emailed when the email changes.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may change only their own email (INV-CEM-1); the shed manager doesn't change neighbors' emails. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the acting neighbor's ID; a request whose neighbor ID isn't the signed-in neighbor's is refused requester-mismatch.
  • PII & compliance: Neighbor Email Changed holds the neighbor's new email address. The old address stays in the earlier events as the shed's record. Names and emails are kept with the shed's history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time email check above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (this slice): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId. Used for INV-CEM-3a (this neighbor's own suspension).
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId. Used for INV-CEM-3a.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId, whileSuspended.
    • These match slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/suspend-neighbor.md and slices/reinstate-neighbor.md. Close Account is specified in a slice being written in depth; it is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Account, Neighbors, Overdue Loans To Notify, Pickup Notices To Send, Undelivered Notices, Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors (the email). Register Neighbor and later Change Email requests check the new email as held.

Open Questions

None.

  • Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors were folded into the Neighbors view (model reshape 2026-11-01, merged-from on slices/neighbors.md v2): reword this doc's mentions of them to Neighbors — v1: v1 keeps the old view names in prose; the views named no longer exist in the model; deferred to v2 (2026-11-01, Mike Key)
"},{"index":6,"name":"My Account — email changed","x0":1134.76,"x1":1278.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: My Account

Intent

Shows a neighbor their own account on the My Account screen: their name, their current email, and whether the account is active, suspended or closed. It is where a neighbor learns they are suspended, and the screen they change their email and close their account from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Account screen. A neighbor whose account is closed can still open it, read-only.
  • Whose account it shows: the account of the neighbor asking. Sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies the neighbor's ID, resolving a person to their newest account, or to their closed one only when they have no newer.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Change Email (Change Email slice) — offered while the account isn't closed (INV-MYAC-9).
    • Close Account (Close Account slice) — offered while the account isn't closed (INV-MYAC-11).

Read Model / View

  • View: My Account built from events: "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the My Account screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. A change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). No action on this screen depends on it being instant, because Change Email and Close Account each check their own rules when they run.

One row per account. A NeighborId is a UUID. An Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Neighbor Registered.neighborId.
name Text Neighbor Registered.name. Never changes.
email Text Neighbor Registered.email, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for this account. Always the current one.
status Text One of active, suspended, closed. Derived: see the status rules below.
canChangeEmail Bool Derived: yes unless status is closed (INV-MYAC-9).
canCloseAccount Bool Derived: yes unless status is closed (INV-MYAC-11).

My Account doesn't show the neighbor's sign-up date; that is the shed manager's to see, on Neighbors.

Status rules. An account's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. closed — Neighbor Account Closed has been recorded for the account. Closed is final.
  2. suspended — otherwise, Neighbor Suspended has been recorded and no Neighbor Reinstated since.
  3. active — otherwise.

Queries

  • Get my account. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns that one account with every field above, or not found if no account has that neighbor ID. It never returns another account (INV-MYAC-1).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-MYAC-1: A neighbor's My Account shows only their own account.
    • The query returns the one account whose neighbor ID it is given, and nothing about any other account.
  • INV-MYAC-2: My Account shows the neighbor's name and their current email.
    • Neighbor Registered sets the email. Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The name never changes after sign-up.
  • INV-MYAC-3: A newly registered neighbor's account shows as active.
    • One account per Neighbor Registered.
  • INV-MYAC-4: A suspended neighbor's account shows as suspended until they are reinstated, and then shows as active again.
    • This is how a neighbor learns they are suspended; they aren't emailed about it.
  • INV-MYAC-5: Once a neighbor closes their account, it shows as closed, permanently.
    • Closed is final. A suspended neighbor who closes their account sees it as closed, not suspended.
  • INV-MYAC-6: After closing their account, the neighbor can still view My Account, read-only.
    • Close Account and Change Email are no longer offered on a closed account.
  • INV-MYAC-7: Only Neighbor Registered, Neighbor Email Changed, Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated and Neighbor Account Closed change My Account.
    • Loans, holds and flags never change it.
  • INV-MYAC-8: A person who signs up again after closing an account has a new account, and My Account shows them only that new account.
    • Each account has its own neighbor ID, and the query returns the one account it is asked for. The old, closed account is no longer shown to them. It stays on the shed manager's Neighbors screen.
  • INV-MYAC-9: My Account offers Change Email on any account that isn't closed.
    • It is offered to a suspended neighbor too. Change Email refuses them with its own reason (INV-CEM-3a, Change Email), and they can change it once reinstated. A refusal with a reason they see means the action was offered.
  • INV-MYAC-10: Applying the same event twice leaves My Account as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYAC-11: My Account offers Close Account on any account that isn't closed.
    • It is offered whether or not the neighbor has tools on loan. Close Account refuses a neighbor with tools on loan with its own reason (INV-CLS-7, Close Account): a refusal with a reason the neighbor sees means the action was offered.
  • INV-MYAC-13: A request with no sign-in is refused before anything else is checked.
  • INV-MYAC-14: My Account is answered only for the signed-in neighbor: a request for any other neighbor ID is refused.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Neighbor registered (INV-MYAC-2, INV-MYAC-3, INV-MYAC-9, INV-MYAC-11)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N1
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for N1, with the name "Ana Ruiz" and the email ana@example.org
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active, with Change Email and Close Account offered.
  • Email changed (INV-MYAC-2)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana.ruiz@example.net, active.
  • Neighbor suspended (INV-MYAC-4, INV-MYAC-9, INV-MYAC-11)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows suspended. Change Email and Close Account are still offered.
  • Neighbor reinstated (INV-MYAC-4)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows suspended
    • When: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows active.
  • Email changed after reinstatement (INV-MYAC-2, INV-MYAC-4)
    • Given: N1 was suspended and then reinstated, and My Account for N1 shows ana@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for N1, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows ana.ruiz@example.net, active.
  • Account closed (INV-MYAC-5, INV-MYAC-6)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows closed, with neither Change Email nor Close Account offered. It can still be read.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-MYAC-5)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows suspended
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 shows closed, not suspended.
  • Signed up again after closing (INV-MYAC-8)
    • Given: account N1, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, is closed, and was not suspended when it was closed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a new account N4, "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org
    • Then: My Account for N4 shows "Ana Ruiz", ana@example.org, active. My Account for N1 still shows closed; asking for N4 never returns N1.
  • Only their own account (INV-MYAC-1)
    • Given: accounts N1 (Ana) and N2 (Ben) are both registered
    • When: My Account is asked for N1
    • Then: it returns Ana's account only. Nothing about Ben's account is returned.
  • Another neighbor's change (INV-MYAC-1, INV-MYAC-7)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for N2
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged.
  • Loans and holds don't change it (INV-MYAC-7)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for N1, and later Hold Placed for N1
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYAC-10)
    • Given: My Account for N1 shows active
    • When: the same Neighbor Registered for N1 is applied again
    • Then: My Account for N1 is unchanged, and there is still one account N1.
  • Asking for an account that doesn't exist (INV-MYAC-1)
    • Given: no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: My Account is asked for N9
    • Then: not found.
  • Not signed in (INV-MYAC-13)
    • Given: nobody is signed in
    • When: My Account is asked for
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.
  • Asked by the wrong person (INV-MYAC-14)
    • Given: Ben (N2) is signed in
    • When: My Account is asked for N1, Ana's account
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only see your own account." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

Reading this view is guarded like a command. A refused read returns nothing and one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown on the screen. The checks run in this order:

  1. not-signed-in (INV-MYAC-13).
  2. requester-mismatch (INV-MYAC-14).
Reason Sentence Rule
not-signed-in Please sign in. INV-MYAC-13
requester-mismatch You can only see your own account. INV-MYAC-14
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYAC-10). An event applied a second time leaves the account as it was after the first.
  • Events for a closed account: closed is final, so no Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated or Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for a closed account (Close Account: nothing reopens, suspends or reinstates a closed account; Change Email, INV-CEM-3). If one reaches this view, it can only be a replay, and it changes nothing.
  • Unknown neighbor ID: the query returns not found. The screen shows that no account was found rather than an error.
  • Stale actions: an action offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, Change Email just after the neighbor was suspended). The command it issues checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may read only their own account (INV-MYAC-1). The query is always asked for the signed-in neighbor's own ID, which sign-in, handled outside the model, supplies; a request for any other neighbor ID is refused requester-mismatch (INV-MYAC-14), and one with no sign-in not-signed-in (INV-MYAC-13).
  • PII & compliance: holds and shows the neighbor's name and email, to that neighbor only. Names and emails are kept with the shed's history and never erased, including a closed account's.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Change Email, Suspend Neighbor, Reinstate Neighbor and Close Account aren't yet written in depth. These names are this view's assumptions; each of those slices is checked against them when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Change Email and Close Account.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":7,"name":"Neighbors — email changed","x0":1303.76,"x1":1447.76,"docHtml":"

Slice: Neighbors

Intent

Shows the shed manager every neighbor account that has signed up, with each account's current status (active, suspended or closed), on the Neighbors screen. It is the shed manager's one screen for neighbors: it shows who the system has flagged for repeated late returns and the late returns behind each flag, who is suspended and since when, and account closures, and it is the screen the shed manager suspends and reinstates neighbors from. The system flags; the shed manager decides.

Version 2 folds the former Flagged Neighbors and Suspended Neighbors views into this one: both were filters of the same accounts, and each offered one action this screen now offers.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Neighbors screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per account ever registered, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. Nothing on this screen records anything by itself; its actions issue commands owned by other slices:
    • Suspend (Suspend Neighbor slice) — offered on every active account, flagged or not (INV-NBRS-6).
    • Reinstate (Reinstate Neighbor slice) — offered on every suspended account (INV-NBRS-13).
  • Flagging is done by the system (Flag Neighbor). A neighbor is not told they were flagged, and a suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag, INV-NTF-7). No email goes to the neighbor on suspension or reinstatement, and no reason or note is recorded with a suspension.
  • Showing only the flagged accounts, or only the suspended ones, is the screen's own filter over this one list; there is no separate read model for either.

Read Model / View

  • View: Neighbors built from events: "Neighbor Registered", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Neighbor Flagged", "Neighbor Suspended", "Neighbor Reinstated", "Neighbor Account Closed", and, to name the late returns behind a flag, "Tool Added", "Tool Checked Out", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned"
  • Consumed by: the Neighbors screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry reflects an event shortly after it is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Suspend and Reinstate check their own rules when they run, so a stale entry can't suspend someone who is no longer active or reinstate someone who is no longer suspended.

One row per account. NeighborId, LoanId and ToolId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded.

Field Type Source / Notes
neighborId NeighborId Neighbor Registered.neighborId.
name Text Neighbor Registered.name. Never changes. Need not be unique.
email Text Neighbor Registered.email, replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed.email for this account. Always the account's current email.
registeredAt Instant Neighbor Registered.registeredAt. Shown as the sign-up date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone (INV-NBRS-5).
status Text One of active, suspended, closed. Derived: see the status rules below.
suspendedAt Instant Derived: suspendedAt of the Neighbor Suspended behind a suspended status; empty otherwise (INV-NBRS-12). Shown as the suspended date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.
flagCount Int Derived: the number of open flags on the account: Neighbor Flagged recorded since the account was last suspended, or ever if never suspended (INV-NBRS-10, INV-NBRS-11). 0 when the account is not flagged.
latestFlaggedAt Instant Derived: flaggedAt of the latest open flag; empty when flagCount is 0. Shown as a date in the shed's local time zone.
lateReturns LateReturn[] Derived: one item for each loan named by the account's open flags, as below; empty when flagCount is 0.
canSuspend Bool Derived: yes while status is active (INV-NBRS-6).
canReinstate Bool Derived: yes while status is suspended (INV-NBRS-13).

Each LateReturn item:

Field Type Source / Notes
loanId LoanId One of Neighbor Flagged.loanIds.
toolName Text Tool Added.name for the loan's tool (Tool Checked Out.toolId).
dueDate Date The loan's due date in force when it was returned: Tool Checked Out.dueDate, replaced by each Loan Extended.dueDate for the loan.
returnedOn Date Tool Returned.returnedOn for the loan.
flaggedAt Instant flaggedAt of the Neighbor Flagged that named this loan.

To fill the late returns when a flag lands, the view also keeps, beyond its rows: every tool's name and, for every loan, its tool, current due date and return date. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned (INV-NBRS-14).

Status rules. An account's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. closed — Neighbor Account Closed has been recorded for the account.
  2. suspended — otherwise, Neighbor Suspended has been recorded and no Neighbor Reinstated since.
  3. active — otherwise.

Flag rules. A flag is open from its Neighbor Flagged until the account is next suspended or closed; suspension and closure clear the account's open flags (INV-NBRS-11). A Neighbor Flagged recorded after a reinstatement starts the account's flags afresh.

Queries

  • List the neighbors. Takes nothing. Returns every account, each with every field above, including its late returns. There is no paging: the query always returns every account, ordered by name, then by registeredAt (INV-NBRS-8). The screen filters to flagged (flagCount above 0) or suspended accounts itself.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-NBRS-1: Every account appears on the Neighbors screen exactly once.
    • One entry per Neighbor Registered; nothing else creates an entry. A neighbor who signs up again after closing their account has a new account, so they appear twice: the closed entry and the new one.
  • INV-NBRS-2: Each account's status is active, suspended or closed, worked out by the status rules above.
    • Neighbor Registered → active. Neighbor Suspended → suspended. Neighbor Reinstated → active. Neighbor Account Closed → closed.
  • INV-NBRS-3: An account that is closed stays listed, shown as closed.
    • This screen is where the shed manager sees account closures. It is the record of every account; a closed account keeps its row, with no action offered and no open flags.
  • INV-NBRS-4: Closed is final.
    • A suspended neighbor who closes their account shows as closed, not suspended. No later event changes a closed account's status.
  • INV-NBRS-5: Each entry shows the account's name, its current email, its sign-up date, and its status.
    • The email is set by Neighbor Registered and replaced by each Neighbor Email Changed. The name never changes.
  • INV-NBRS-6: The screen offers Suspend on every active account, whether or not the neighbor has been flagged, and on no other.
    • Suspend Neighbor checks its own rules when it runs.
  • INV-NBRS-8: Accounts are listed by name, ignoring case, then by when they signed up.
    • So a neighbor who signed up again after closing appears twice, the older account first.
  • INV-NBRS-7: Applying the same event twice leaves the Neighbors screen as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-NBRS-9: Only the shed manager can read the Neighbors screen.
    • A signed-in caller without the shed-manager role is refused with not-shed-manager, and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned to either.
  • INV-NBRS-10: A flagged account shows how many open flags it has, the date of the latest, and the late returns behind every open flag, each with the tool's name, its due date, the date it was returned, and the date of the flag that named it.
    • Neighbor Flagged names the late returns it uses up, as the loans they belong to. It carries no copies of names or dates. The view looks those loans up in the loan events it hears: the tool from Tool Checked Out and its name from Tool Added, the due date from Tool Checked Out as moved by any Loan Extended, and the return date from Tool Returned.
    • Being flagged never suspends anyone by itself, and there is no dismiss action: a flag the shed manager decides not to act on stays open.
  • INV-NBRS-11: Suspending or closing the account clears its open flags; a flag recorded after a reinstatement starts the count afresh.
    • The flags were what the shed manager acted on, or can no longer act on. A suspended neighbor is never flagged (Neighbors To Flag), so no flag lands while suspended.
  • INV-NBRS-12: A suspended account shows when it was suspended; the date is cleared on reinstatement.
    • A suspension never lifts by itself after a set time, and it is never permanent. A neighbor suspended again after a reinstatement shows the new date.
  • INV-NBRS-13: The screen offers Reinstate on every suspended account, and on no other.
    • Reinstate Neighbor checks its own rules when it runs.
  • INV-NBRS-14: To name late returns, the view keeps every tool's name and every loan's tool, current due date and return date, whether or not the borrower is flagged; none of it is returned on its own.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org and Ben Ito with ben@example.org. Ana returned the ladder (L1, due 31 August) on 1 September, the drill (L2, due 15 September) on 20 September and the hedge trimmer (L3, due 1 October) on 5 October, all late.

  • Neighbor registered (INV-NBRS-1, INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-5, INV-NBRS-6)
    • Given: no neighbors have signed up
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, signed up on today's date, as active, not flagged, with Suspend offered and Reinstate not offered.
  • Two neighbors with the same name (INV-NBRS-1)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a different account, also named Ana Ruiz, with ana.r@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists both, as separate entries.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-NBRS-7)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana once, as active
    • When: the same Neighbor Registered for Ana is applied again
    • Then: the Neighbors screen still lists Ana once.
  • Email changed (INV-NBRS-5)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz with ana@example.org, as active
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists Ana Ruiz with ana.ruiz@example.net, still active.
  • Neighbor flagged (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana as active, not flagged
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 5 October, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active, flagged once, latest on 5 October, with three late returns: the ladder (due 31 August, returned 1 September), the drill (due 15 September, returned 20 September) and the hedge trimmer (due 1 October, returned 5 October). Suspend is offered, as before.
  • Due date after an extension (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: L2 was extended from 15 September to 18 September before it was returned on 20 September
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana, naming L1, L2 and L3
    • Then: the drill's late return shows due 18 September, returned 20 September.
  • Flagged again (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged once on 5 October, and she has since returned three more tools late (L4, L5, L6)
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 15 November, naming L4, L5 and L6
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged twice, latest on 15 November, with all six late returns: L1, L2 and L3 flagged 5 October, and L4, L5 and L6 flagged 15 November.
  • Flag left alone (INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has shown Ana flagged since 5 October, and the shed manager has not suspended her
    • When: a month passes with no Neighbor Suspended recorded for Ana
    • Then: Ana is still shown flagged once, with the same late returns.
  • Flagged neighbor changes their email (INV-NBRS-5, INV-NBRS-10)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, flagged once
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz, ana.ruiz@example.net. Her flags are unchanged.
  • Neighbor suspended (INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-11, INV-NBRS-12, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active, flagged once, and Ben as active
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana on 7 October
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 7 October, with no open flags, Suspend not offered and Reinstate offered. Ben is unchanged.
  • Suspended without a flag (INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-12)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ben as active, not flagged
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ben on 9 October
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ben as suspended since 9 October, with Reinstate offered.
  • Neighbor reinstated (INV-NBRS-2, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-12, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 7 October
    • When: Neighbor Reinstated is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as active again, with no suspended date, not flagged, with Suspend offered and Reinstate not offered.
  • Flagged again after reinstatement (INV-NBRS-11)
    • Given: Ana was flagged, then suspended, which cleared her flags, and later reinstated
    • When: Neighbor Flagged is recorded for Ana on 20 January, naming L7, L8 and L9
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana flagged once, latest on 20 January, with only L7, L8 and L9.
  • Suspended again after reinstatement (INV-NBRS-12)
    • Given: Ana was suspended on 7 October and reinstated on 1 November
    • When: Neighbor Suspended is recorded for Ana again on 3 February
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended since 3 February.
  • Account closed (INV-NBRS-3, INV-NBRS-6, INV-NBRS-11)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana as active, flagged once
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen still lists Ana, now shown as closed, with no open flags and neither Suspend nor Reinstate offered.
  • Suspended neighbor closes their account (INV-NBRS-4, INV-NBRS-13)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as suspended
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ana
    • Then: the Neighbors screen shows Ana as closed, with Reinstate not offered.
  • Closed stays closed (INV-NBRS-4)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana's account as closed
    • When: an earlier Neighbor Suspended, Neighbor Reinstated or Neighbor Flagged for that account is applied again
    • Then: the account is still shown as closed, with no open flags.
  • Signing up again after closing (INV-NBRS-1, INV-NBRS-3)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen shows Ana Ruiz's account, ana@example.org, as closed
    • When: Neighbor Registered is recorded for a new account for Ana Ruiz, with ana@example.org
    • Then: the Neighbors screen lists two entries for Ana Ruiz with ana@example.org: the old account, still closed, and the new one, active, with Suspend offered.
  • Listing order (INV-NBRS-8)
    • Given: Ben Ito signed up on 2 October; Ana Ruiz signed up on 1 October, closed her account, and signed up again on 5 October
    • When: the shed manager lists the neighbors
    • Then: the accounts come back as: Ana Ruiz (signed up 1 October, closed), Ana Ruiz (signed up 5 October, active), then Ben Ito.
  • Listing the neighbors
    • Given: the Neighbors screen lists Ana (active, flagged once), Ben (suspended) and Cara (closed)
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists the neighbors
    • Then: all three are returned with all their fields, Ana's with her late returns, with no paging. Only Ana's entry offers Suspend; only Ben's offers Reinstate.
  • A neighbor tries to read the list (INV-NBRS-9)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has entries
    • When: a neighbor, signed in without the shed-manager role, asks for the neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see this screen." Nothing is returned.
  • No sign-in (INV-NBRS-9)
    • Given: the Neighbors screen has entries
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the neighbors
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller without the shed-manager role with not-shed-manager ("Only the shed manager can see this screen."), and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal. These mean the same conditions as in the shed manager's commands.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-NBRS-7). An event applied a second time leaves the entry as it was after the first.
  • Event for an account the view hasn't seen: events are applied in the order they were recorded, and every account starts with Neighbor Registered, so this can't happen.
  • Events on a closed account: a Neighbor Flagged, Neighbor Suspended or Neighbor Reinstated applied to a closed account changes nothing (INV-NBRS-4).
  • Stale actions: Suspend or Reinstate offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, on a neighbor who has just closed their account). Suspend Neighbor and Reinstate Neighbor check their own rules and refuse with their own reasons; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Neighbors screen is the shed manager's alone; neighbors see only their own account, on My Account. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; only a caller with it may read this view.
  • PII & compliance: shows every account's name, current email, sign-up date, status, suspension date and late-return history to the shed manager, including closed accounts, which stay listed. A replaced email is not kept in the view. To name late returns, the view keeps every tool's name and every loan's tool and dates, whether or not the borrower is flagged. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and are never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId, name, email, registeredAt.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Neighbor Flagged (Flag Neighbor): neighborId, loanIds (LoanId[]), flaggedAt.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId, suspendedAt.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId, returnedOn.
    • These keys match slices/register-neighbor.md, flag-neighbor.md, suspend-neighbor.md and the loan slices' docs.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Suspend Neighbor and Reinstate Neighbor.
  • Lineage: v2 merges Flagged Neighbors v1 and Suspended Neighbors v1 into this view (model reshape, 2026-11-01). Their docs stay in slices/ marked superseded by neighbors@v2.

Open Questions

None.
